sentences.text: The instant petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 657/2018 registered at Police Station Nand Nagri, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Anand V. Khatri, learned ASC (Crl.) accepts notice on behalf of the State.

3. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr.
Hitesh Pandey and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Gaurav Yadav from Police Station Nand Nagri,
Delhi.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were married on 18.02.2017 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
Due to some temperamental differences, the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 were not able to live together and have been living separately since 19.06.2017.

The respondent no. 2 lodged a complaint with the Crime Against Women Cell, Nand Nagari, Delhi by levelling allegations of demand of dowry and cruelties against petitioners and subsequently, this complaint culminated into registration of an FIR bearing no.
657/2018 at Police Station Nand Nagari, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498a/406/34 of IPC.

entities.text: Crime Against Women Cell, Nand Nagari, Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is stated that both the parties have amicably settled the matter before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi on 22.03.2022.
5.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, on 22.03.2022.
6.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

7. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 50,000/- today, i.e., 18.05.2023 vide DD No. 035660 drawn on HDFC Bank,
Kashmeri Gate, Delhi and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:17:45 8.

In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

9. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 657/2018 registered at Police Station Nand Nagri, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
10. The present petition stands disposed of.
11. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
